items.title: The preimage of a scheme theoretically dense open under a flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite morphism is scheme theoretically dense
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme W of S and a morphism of schemes f : X -> S which is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, the preimage f^{-1}(W) is scheme theoretically dense in X (source lines 3421-3429). The proof uses the characterization of scheme theoretic density by functions vanishing on the open: given an open V and g in O_V(V) restricting to zero on f^{-1}(W) intersect V, one assumes g nonzero and applies the go-down-with-annihilators lemma to shrink V and find U in S with a quasi-coherent subsheaf F of O_U, an integer r and an injection F^{oplus r} -> pi_*O_V containing g; the components g_i then vanish on W intersect U because g does, and vanish identically because W is scheme theoretically dense, forcing g = 0.
